reader.requirement: At --std 85 (with the 1989 Intrinsic Function amendment) the compiler must accept FUNCTION REM followed by a parenthesized list of exactly two arguments (literals, identifiers including subscripted ones, arithmetic expressions, nested function-identifiers, separated by spaces or ', '), used in an arithmetic expression, and refuse the form with fewer or more arguments, no argument list, or an empty '( )'.

edition-consulted.switches: the D8 window sig.IntroducedIn > DialectLevel; REM's row (IntrinsicCatalog Build) carries IntroducedIn 85, so 85 passes like 2023
an empty argument list '( )' is refused below 2002 (function-empty-argument-list-2002, COBOL0900)
a numeric function-identifier outside an arithmetic expression is refused below 2002 (NumericFunctionIdentifierOperand2002, COBOL0900)

reader.edition-search: grep Edition|DialectLevel|IntroducedIn in IntrinsicBinder.cs and IntrinsicCatalog.cs; grep functionCall in VersionConformancePass.cs; the arity check (MinArgs/MaxArgs 2/2) has no edition arm
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: at 85 FUNCTION REM is admitted only inside an arithmetic expression and '( )' draws an additional 2002-introduction refusal; the two-argument format itself is the same at every edition
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_f39_02 covers space and comma separators, literal, signed item, decimal item and expression arguments; not exercised: subscripted and nested function arguments, the 18-digit extreme, and the refusal of 0, 1 or 3 arguments

probes.printed: COBOL1504 FUNCTION REM takes 2 argument(s); 1 given / 3 given / 0 given, plus COBOL0900 empty function argument list '( )' requires COBOL-2002
probes.expected: the format admits exactly two arguments

probes.printed: COBOL1504: FUNCTION REM takes 2 argument(s); 0 given
probes.expected: FUNCTION REM with no argument list is refused

probes.printed: COBOL0900: a numeric or integer function-identifier where an identifier is written (not in an arithmetic expression) requires COBOL-2002, for MOVE and DISPLAY
probes.expected: §1985:IV.4.3.8.3.3 SR4: a numeric function may be used only in an arithmetic expression

reader.notes: The grammar's functionCall takes any argument list; the catalog row (REM, Fixed 2..2, IntroducedIn 85) drives the arity check in BindFunctionResult, so every count other than two is refused with COBOL1504. The values follow the truncating INTEGER-PART definition, including a negative 18-digit argument-1 and a negative argument-2.

refuter.evidence: refute-1985-230/r5a.cob at --std 85: FUNCTION REM (7 -2) -> 1.00, (A -2) -> 1.00, (-7 +2) -> -1.00, (A, +3) -> 1.00, REM(17 5) with no space before '(' -> 2.00: a signed literal after a space is argument-2, not a binary minus (1985 binary operators need spaces on both sides). r5b.cob: a data item named REM (function names are not reserved in the 1989 amendment) used as argument-1 inside FUNCTION REM (REM E (1)) -> 9.00; expression arguments with ';' and ',' separators (E (2) * 5 ; E (3)) -> 2.00, (REM / 2 , E (3) - 1) -> 0.50. All match RV1 argument-1 - (argument-2 * INTEGER-PART(argument-1 / argument-2)). cite.py: OK  §1989:A.2.37.2  (2.37.2 General Format)  the text is in the clause.
